Pledging with allies to send more Patriot interceptors to help protect Ukraine, he stressed that “every additional missile saves the lives of our people.” More drone attack warnings from Kyiv were going live this morning. Responding to the overnight attacks, Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko declared Friday a day of mourning in the city. I will bring you more updates throughout the day. It’s Thursday, 20 August 2026, it’s Jakub Krupa here, and this is Europe Live. Romania’s military has destroyed a marine drone spotted just “a few hundred meters” from the Neptun Deep platform, a major offshore gas project in the Black Sea. The drone, spotted just “a few hundreds of meters” from the gas extraction works at the Neptun Deep platform located some 80 miles east of the city of Constanța, was destroyed by a Romanian F-16 fighter jet.

“Following the analyses carried out and in coordination with the President of Romania, in order to protect the lives of the several hundred people working on the platform and to secure the critical infrastructure, the decision was made to destroy the drone,” Romania’s defence minister Radu Miruță said in a post on Facebook. Miruță added that Romanian officials confirmed with Kyiv that the vessel was “not of Ukrainian origin,” strongly suggesting Russian involvement amid heightened maritime tensions in the region. Earlier this month, Romanian army divers destroyed two Gerbera-type drones drifting in the ⁠country’s Black Sea exclusive economic zone near the same offshore gas project. At least 12 people were killed and 40 injured in a series of Russian attacks on the Ukrainian capital of Kyiv. “It was a massive attack – the Russians had been preparing for a long time, combining different types of ballistic missiles, cruise missiles, and drones, aiming to cause as much damage as possible to civilian infrastructure. There is destruction in Kyiv and the region, as well as in the Odesa and Chernihiv regions,” Ukraine’s president Volodymyr Zelenskyy said. The attack will likely draw further attention to Ukraine’s shortage of air defence missiles. “While Moscow is investing in ballistic missiles and escalation, such strikes do not always receive the response they should from the world. And as long as Ukraine does not have enough anti-ballistic defence, Russia will not consider peace seriously,” Zelenskyy warned this morning.

At least 12 people were killed and 40 injured in a series of Russian attacks on the Ukrainian capital of Kyiv.

“It was a massive attack – the Russians had been preparing for a long time, combining different types of ballistic missiles, cruise missiles, and drones, aiming to cause as much damage as possible to civilian infrastructure. There is destruction in Kyiv and the region, as well as in the Odesa and Chernihiv regions,” Ukraine’s president Volodymyr Zelenskyy said.

The attack will likely draw further attention to Ukraine’s shortage of air defence missiles.

“While Moscow is investing in ballistic missiles and escalation, such strikes do not always receive the response they should from the world. And as long as Ukraine does not have enough anti-ballistic defence, Russia will not consider peace seriously,” Zelenskyy warned this morning.

Pledging with allies to send more Patriot interceptors to help protect Ukraine, he stressed that “every additional missile saves the lives of our people.”

More drone attack warnings from Kyiv were going live this morning.

Responding to the overnight attacks, Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko declared Friday a day of mourning in the city.

I will bring you more updates throughout the day.

It’s Thursday, 20 August 2026, it’s Jakub Krupa here, and this is Europe Live.

Romania’s military has destroyed a marine drone spotted just “a few hundred meters” from the Neptun Deep platform, a major offshore gas project in the Black Sea.

The drone, spotted just “a few hundreds of meters” from the gas extraction works at the Neptun Deep platform located some 80 miles east of the city of Constanța, was destroyed by a Romanian F-16 fighter jet.

“Following the analyses carried out and in coordination with the President of Romania, in order to protect the lives of the several hundred people working on the platform and to secure the critical infrastructure, the decision was made to destroy the drone,” Romania’s defence minister Radu Miruță said in a post on Facebook.

Miruță added that Romanian officials confirmed with Kyiv that the vessel was “not of Ukrainian origin,” strongly suggesting Russian involvement amid heightened maritime tensions in the region.

Earlier this month, Romanian army divers destroyed two Gerbera-type drones drifting in the ⁠country’s Black Sea exclusive economic zone near the same offshore gas project.

The death toll from the overnight Russian attack on Kyiv has gone up to 15, Kyiv authorities said.
